Deeptime

Exploring reefs in detail

Explore the work

ProjectsResearchExpeditionsDiscuss a project

Deeptime is a prototype web viewer for streaming and inspecting gigabyte-scale reef orthomosaics: detailed maps assembled from underwater photographs.

I built it alongside the processing workflow for the Bonaire Baseline surveys, connecting imagery collected in the field with a way to explore the resulting reef maps in a browser.

My contribution: survey equipment and methods, automated image processing, and prototype viewer development.

Status: prototype.

The problem

A reef survey produces thousands of photographs. Turning those images into a useful map requires a sequence of processing steps; making the map accessible introduces another challenge when the output is gigabytes in size.

From photographs to maps

I built a pipeline using Python and Agisoft Metashape to automate image ingestion, quality screening, camera alignment, 3D reconstruction, orthomosaic generation, and GIS export.

Operator checkpoints preserve opportunities for measurements and review during processing.

From maps to exploration

Deeptime provides a browser interface for streaming and inspecting the resulting orthomosaics. The prototype connects the survey outputs with a practical way to explore their detail.

The survey behind the software

The 2026 Bonaire campaign produced 70,885 source images across 18 reef sites, mapping approximately 34,160 m² of reef.
